intro: Helsinki rewards visitors with compact streets, ferries to fortress islands and a calm sea-facing calm. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: HSL runs metro, trams, buses, local trains and the Suomenlinna ferry on one ticket system.
Buy tickets by contactless card, HSL app or R kiosk; cash is not accepted on board.
Airport trains need an ABC ticket; city centre travel needs AB.
Taxis wait at ranks and the airport; ride apps like Bolt and Uber operate in Helsinki.
Driving is easy but parking is costly; walking and trams cover the centre well.
Bikes are popular in summer; city bike stations are widespread.

helsinki_cathedral.name: Helsinki Cathedral
helsinki_cathedral.tip: Climb the steps for the best free view over Senate Square, then look inside for the plain white interior.

suomenlinna.name: Suomenlinna Sea Fortress
suomenlinna.price_text: Island free · ferry about EUR 5 return (HSL ticket)
suomenlinna.hours: Island always open · ferry runs through the day, roughly 06:00–02:00
suomenlinna.tip: Take the HSL ferry from Market Square and allow at least half a day to walk the walls and museums.

temppeliaukio.name: Temppeliaukio Church (Rock Church)
temppeliaukio.price_text: About EUR 8 adult · check current price
temppeliaukio.hours: Usually daily, roughly 10:00–17:00 (varies by season and services)
temppeliaukio.tip: Built into solid rock with a copper roof. Go early or late to avoid the midday crowds.

uspenski.name: Uspenski Cathedral
uspenski.tip: Red-brick Orthodox cathedral on the hill above Market Square. Quiet inside, so dress modestly.

canal_route.name: Beautiful Canal Route (boat cruise)
canal_route.price_text: About EUR 20–30 adult · check operator and season
canal_route.hours: Summer season only, several departures daily (check on the day)
canal_route.tip: Sightseeing boats leave from Market Square. Book a seat in advance on sunny summer days.

opera.name: Finnish National Opera
opera.price_text: Tickets vary widely, roughly EUR 20–90 · check programme
opera.hours: Performance evenings; box office daytime (check on the day)
opera.tip: Book online ahead. Cheaper seats still give a good view of the stage.

karjalanpaisti.name: Karjalanpaisti (Karelian stew)
karjalanpaisti.price_text: About EUR 15–25 as a main course
karjalanpaisti.hours: Depends on the restaurant; lunch and dinner
karjalanpaisti.tip: A slow-cooked beef and pork stew. Try it at a traditional lunch restaurant with mashed potatoes.

linnanmaki.name: Linnanmäki Amusement Park
linnanmaki.price_text: Free entry · ride wristband roughly EUR 40–50 · check on the day
linnanmaki.tip: Entry is free; you pay for rides. Buy the wristband if you plan more than a few rides.

national_museum.name: National Museum of Finland
national_museum.price_text: About EUR 12–16 adult · under 18 free · check on the day
national_museum.tip: Good rainy-day stop. The building itself, with its frescoes, is worth a look.

oodi.name: Oodi Helsinki Central Library
oodi.tip: Go up to the top floor for the curved wooden reading room and free city views.

planet_funfun.name: Planet FunFun (Fanfaari)
planet_funfun.price_text: About EUR 10–20 per child · check on the day
planet_funfun.hours: Daily, daytime hours (check on the day)
planet_funfun.tip: Indoor play centre for young children. Confirm opening hours and prices before you go.

sibelius.name: Sibelius Monument
sibelius.tip: Steel pipes in Sibelius Park. Combine with a walk along the nearby seafront.

market_square.name: Market Square (Kauppatori)
market_square.price_text: Free to browse · snacks roughly EUR 5–15
market_square.hours: Roughly Mon–Sat 06:30–18:00 · summer longer (check on the day)
market_square.tip: Try salmon soup or a berry pastry from a stall. Ferries to Suomenlinna leave from here.

old_market_hall.name: Old Market Hall (Vanha Kauppahalli)
old_market_hall.hours: Mon–Sat roughly 08:00–18:00 · closed Sunday (check on the day)
old_market_hall.tip: Covered food hall near Market Square. Good for a quick lunch and local cheeses.

esplanadi.name: Esplanadi Park
esplanadi.tip: Central green strip between the harbour and the shops. Sit on a bench and watch the city go by.

kallio_walk.name: Kallio neighbourhood walk
kallio_walk.hours: Always open; bars busiest in the evening
kallio_walk.tip: Walk from Hakaniemi through Kallio for street art, cafés and a local feel away from the centre.

tram_tour.name: Helsinki tram sightseeing ride
tram_tour.price_text: Single HSL ticket about EUR 3 · day ticket available
tram_tour.hours: Trams run from early morning to late evening
tram_tour.tip: A cheap way to see the city. Buy a day ticket if you plan several rides.

seurasaari.name: Seurasaari Open-Air Museum
seurasaari.price_text: Island free · museum buildings about EUR 10 (check on the day)
seurasaari.hours: Summer season mainly; island open year-round
seurasaari.tip: Wooden houses on a forested island. Walk the island for free even when buildings are closed.

cafe_regatta.name: Café Regatta
cafe_regatta.hours: Daytime hours, roughly 09:00–20:00 in summer (check on the day)
cafe_regatta.tip: Waterfront café near Sibelius Park. Good stop on a seaside walk.

loyly.name: Löyly sauna and restaurant
loyly.price_text: Sauna roughly EUR 15–25 · towel and food extra
loyly.hours: Daily, long hours (check on the day)
loyly.tip: Seaside sauna with a terrace. Book ahead at weekends and bring a swimsuit.

hakaniemi_hall.name: Hakaniemi Market Hall
hakaniemi_hall.hours: Mon–Sat daytime · closed Sunday (check on the day)
hakaniemi_hall.tip: Local food hall with cheap lunch counters. Pair it with a walk into Kallio.

stays.why: Central and walkable: main station, trams and the big sights are minutes away.
Quiet old streets near the cathedral and Market Square; good for first-time sightseeing.
Livelier and cheaper, with bars and cafés; a short tram or metro ride to the centre.
Bus and metro hub under one roof; handy for day trips and late arrivals.

food: Try Finnish basics: salmon soup (lohikeitto), rye bread and Karelian pasties.
Market Square (Kauppatori) stalls sell snacks and berries in season; check opening hours on the day.
Lunch is often cheaper than dinner; look for weekday lunch offers in the centre.
Cafés serve cinnamon buns (korvapuusti) and strong filter coffee; Finns drink a lot of it.
Book popular restaurants ahead on weekends; many kitchens close earlier than in bigger cities.
more_time: Take the ferry to Suomenlinna and give the fortress half a day.
Day-trip to Porvoo old town by bus; check timetables on the day.
In summer, hop a ferry to an island like Pihlajasaari for a swim and a walk.
